newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep. Gephardt slams Gingrich tax proposal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep. Gephardt slams Gingrich tax proposal.

text.p: House Minority Leader Dick Gephardt Thursday accused House Speaker Newt Gingrich of pandering to the far right by calling for elimination of capital gains and estate taxes this year.

Telling reporters that Democrats would fight such plans, Gephardt said it appeared the speaker's proposal, announced Wednesday, was an effort to "rehabilitate his image with the right wing of the Republican party."
Gephardt complained the proposal would favor the wealthy at a time when Republicans were holding up legislation to provide some economic relief to the middle class.

Gingrich has come under fire from conservatives in his own party who are frustrated by the slow pace of the House this year. They were also angered by the speaker's earlier suggestion that Republicans might need to delay a tax cut until a balanced budget deal was reached.
Wednesday Gingrich said Republicans would push for a major tax cutting package this year.

Gephardt also criticized House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, an Ohio Republican, who said the White House will have to put forward deeper cuts in discretionary spending programs in order to reach a balanced budget deal.

"The House Republicans are not willing to pass a budget that doesn't have large, unjustified tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans that have to be paid for with cuts in education and health care," Gephardt said.
He said President Clinton had shown flexibility on the budget, but Republicans had been unwilling to make concessions, or even draft their own budget plan.
"The president has been compromising, he's the only one out there with a budget," Gephardt said.
He warned that Democrats would not support any move to require Medicare beneficiaries to pay higher premiums.

He also said House Democrats were trying to craft a bill to provide health insurance for kids that could be funded through an increase in the federal tobacco tax, but cautioned that no final decision had been made.
